title: Avoiding Sanitary Tees in Horizontal Drainage Transitions
description: Using a standard sanitary tee to transition horizontal drainage flow into another horizontal pipe is a frequent installation mistake. A sanitary tee has a short sweep designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal or horizontal-to-vertical drops where gravity aids direction. When placed flat on a horizontal line, wastewater lacks the momentum to sweep cleanly through the junction, causing waste solids to accumulate and slow down flow velocity. This often leads to frequent blockages and sluggish drainage. Professional installers use combination wye and eighth-bend fittings or long-sweep tees to maintain continuous, smooth flow direction along horizontal drain lines.

Avoiding Sanitary Tees in Horizontal Drainage Transitions

Using a standard sanitary tee to transition horizontal drainage flow into another horizontal pipe is a frequent installation mistake. A sanitary tee has a short sweep designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal or horizontal-to-vertical drops where gravity aids direction. When placed flat on a horizontal line, wastewater lacks the momentum to sweep cleanly through the junction, causing waste solids to accumulate and slow down flow velocity. This often leads to frequent blockages and sluggish drainage. Professional installers use combination wye and eighth-bend fittings or long-sweep tees to maintain continuous, smooth flow direction along horizontal drain lines.
